messages:
maria: Seeing intermittent 30-60% packet loss on internal L4 VIP traffic between rack-3 and rack-7 since ~09:10 UTC. Affects model shard syncs and causes GPU workers to stall.
ajay: On it. Any recent LB changes?
maria: Not from our side. deploy-bot posted a canary update at 08:55 but it was a config tweak (idle timeout).
deploy-bot: canary-l4-config rolled to rack-3 at 08:55 by ops-ci (CI job #1247). :information_source:
sam_k: I grabbed tcpdumps. Seeing lots of retransmits + duplicate acks on flows that go through ToR-7 -> ToR-3 path. Sample: 
```
14:23:11.123456 IP 10.10.3.21.34567 > 10.10.7.19.443: Flags [.], ack 12345, win 64240, length 0
14:23:11.223789 IP 10.10.3.21.34567 > 10.10.7.19.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12500, ack 9999, win 64240, length 155
14:23:11.323999 IP 10.10.3.21.34567 > 10.10.7.19.443: TCP Retransmission
```
\sam_k: Can we reproduce without LB in path? I started iperf UDP and saw lower loss on direct rack-to-rack path when bypassing LB by hitting pod IP directly. When going via VIP/L4, loss spikes.
maria: That suggests L4 load balancer + ToR interaction. The LB does 2-tuple hashing and SNAT for connections routed across racks. Conntrack entries show SNAT happening: `conntrack -L | grep 10.10.7.19` lots of TIME_WAIT.
ajay: Conntrack table sizes okay? Could conntrack exhaustion cause asymmetric NATing?
emily: Conntrack at 30% usage, nothing alarming. But I do see a bunch of flows with NAT'ed IPs that get rehashed to different ToRs mid-flow when one ToR returns ICMP redirect? Not sure.
sam_k: I dumped iptables/nat and saw duplication where LB created ephemeral SNAT on exit node. Packets come back with different MAC from another ToR then switch gets confused.\maria: Ops suggestion: enable ARP suppression (again) on ToR-3 and roll back the fw on ToR-7 to 12.3? Concerned about rollback risk.
ajay: Alternative short-term mitigation: force LB to stick by source IP + port (4-tuple) so that flows don't get hashed across ToRs. Also pin service backends to same rack for critical shards.
emily: I can push sticky hashing for l4-vip-prod and increase conntrack timeout to reduce churn.
sam_k: Also recommend disabling large segment offload (GSO/GRO) cluster-wide for a quick test; seems to reduce visible retransmits.
maria: Can someone run `ethtool -k` on ToR-facing host and paste output?
ajay: On host gpu-03-r3: `ethtool -k eth0` -> "generic-segmentation-offload: on\nlarge-receive-offload: on\n`"
sam_k: ToR-7 config excerpt shows 'enable storm-control' and 'arp-suppression on'; there's also a known vendor bug where LRO+ARP suppression causes mid-flow drops when SNAT is used.
emily: Filed vendor ticket with fw team (case# VND-90842). They acknowledged pattern and suggested firmware rollback or disabling ARP suppression.
maria: Rolling change now: emily, please flip LB sticky hashing and increase conntrack timeout; sam_k disable GSO on test nodes, ajay coordinate ToR fw rollback window with network team.
emily: Pushing sticky hashing now. Will post when done.
ops-bot: l4-config: sticky-hash enabled for l4-vip-prod by emily at 09:47 UTC.
emily: Conntrack timeout bumped from 60s->300s.
sam_k: Disabled GSO/GRO on gpu-03-r3 and gpu-07-r19. Early numbers: packet loss down from ~40%->6% and p50 latency back to ~5ms.
ajay: Good. I'll hold rollback until vendor confirms root cause or we have a staged change window.
maria: For next steps: 1) schedule ToR firmware rollback or vendor patch, 2) evaluate cluster-wide offload policy (default disable for LB-facing NICs), 3) leave sticky hashing + increased conntrack as fallback.
sam_k: Also add an alert for intra-rack packet retransmit delta > 10% (currently only p50/p95 latency alerts).
emily: I'll create the rollout PR and include test plan to validate RDMA unaffected.
maria: Thanks team. Keep thread updated. If loss recurs, attach tcpdump + `ethtool -S` from both ToRs.
ajay: Noted. Will monitor.
(09:57 UTC) emily: sticky-hash confirmed, metrics stable for 10m.
(10:31 UTC) ops-bot: incident-note: temporary mitigation applied (sticky-hash + conntrack timeout + GSO off on 2 hosts).
